docs.title: Dungeon Shooter Maker
docs.text: Dungeon Shooter Maker is a toolkit for making top-down, room-by-room dungeon shooters in Unity without writing code. Guns, items, enemies, bosses, rooms, floors and the reward economy are all data, edited in dedicated windows and tested with one click.

docs.title: What ships with the package
docs.text:
The package ships with a complete sample game: 4 floors and a camp lobby, 4 heroes, 16 guns, 24 items, 12 enemies and 6 bosses, 12 synergies, 38 upgrades, 33 rooms, chests, shops and shrines. Change it, or use it as a reference for your own game.

Everything is a ScriptableObject asset in Assets/DungeonShooterMaker/Content/Default/ and is listed in the Content Database (Resources/DungeonShooterMaker/DefaultContent). Editors create, rename, duplicate and delete those assets for you and keep the database list up to date.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Follow the quick start to play the sample and change one value.
  2. Learn what each window makes in The editors.
  3. Set the run's rules, offers, elites and lobby in Run rules and progression.
  4. Build enemies, rooms, floors, props and mini-bosses in Content and gameplay.
  5. Add tracks, sounds and effect animations in Music and sound.
  6. Check tests, Project Check and common problems in FAQ and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Tested environment
docs.text:
• Unity 6 (the sample project is on 6000.0.47f1) with the Universal Render Pipeline (URP 17.0.4).
  • Heroes, enemies, guns, effects and UI frames ship as sprite sheets; floors, walls and props are drawn from small pixel maps in code. Your own sprites are optional (see Your own art).
  • Game text uses the pixel font Galmuri (Galmuri7, Galmuri9, Galmuri11 Bold, English and Korean), which may ship with your game under the SIL Open Font License. See Support and licenses.

docs.title: How the manual is organised
docs.text:
• Start here — welcome and quick start.
  • Making your game — the editor windows, run rules, content and gameplay, music and sound.
  • Help — testing, Project Check, design notes, FAQ and support.

The pages are maintained prose taken from the package's Documentation/UserGuide.md; building this site does not require Unity or the product source.

docs.title: Content and gameplay
docs.text: This page covers the content model, how content gets into a build, and the gameplay pieces that are not a window of their own: elites and mini-bosses, props, pits, gates, challenge rooms, the shopkeeper, languages and the balance report.

docs.title: How content works
docs.text:
Each piece of content is a ScriptableObject asset (Assets/DungeonShooterMaker/Content/Default/...) listed in the Content Database (Resources/DungeonShooterMaker/DefaultContent). Editors create, rename, duplicate and delete these assets for you and keep the database list up to date.

  • Every asset has an id (lower case, used for references) and a name (shown to the player).
  • Editors check your data as you type. Problems show at the top of the form, and the game never loads broken data: it reports the problem and skips that entry.
  • Undo works for every edit.
  • Project Overview ▸ Check project finds design problems the per-asset check cannot see (see Project Check).

docs.title: Mods and JSON
docs.text:
The whole database can be exported to JSON folders (Export JSON…) and imported back (Import JSON…).

A built game also reads JSON from Application.persistentDataPath/content/ (or a folder passed with -content <dir>): files there override default content by id, so players can mod your game without Unity.

Folder names: guns, enemies, rooms, floors, items, statuses, loot, chests, shops, shrines, characters, synergies plus ruleset.json. To see every field, export the sample with Export JSON…: the files use the same names as the editors.

docs.title: Elite modifiers
docs.text:
An elite is a normal enemy that spawns with one modifier, made in Tools > Dungeon Shooter Maker > Enemy Modifier Editor. A modifier has:

  • a prefix, shown before the enemy name,
  • multipliers for health, speed, fire delay and damage (they multiply on top of the floor difficulty, like the old hexed numbers),
  • extra bullet patterns that join every volley ("add") or replace the state's own ("replace"),
  • an aura of effect blocks that runs while the hero is close (the same words a boss phase uses: bullets and damage hit the hero, heal heals the elite; at most once a second),
  • a sprite tint (the outline colour and width are stored for the art pass),
  • extra coins, hearts and a loot table,
  • an appear animation.

One modifier per enemy; bosses and mini-bosses are skipped unless you allow bosses.

docs.title: When elites appear
docs.text:
Run Rules > Elites sets the base chance, a guaranteed number per floor, whether bosses can be elite, a chance-by-curse curve (empty = the old hexed curve) and a weighted pool of modifiers (empty = the built-in hexed one).

A floor can add its own chance and pool in the Floor Editor, a difficulty has Elite chance +, a room has Extra elite chance in this room, and an encounter line with Elite on always spawns elites (a wave of them). Rolls use the floor's seed, so -seed reproduces the same elites.

Run Rules > Hexed enemies still exists for old content: its numbers become the built-in hexed modifier (no name prefix and the old "hexed enemy appears" effect, so old enemies look the same), and Convert these numbers to a hexed modifier asset turns them into a real one you can edit. See Run rules and progression.

docs.title: Mini-bosses
docs.text:
A mini-boss is not a boss: it is a normal enemy shown with the boss health bar.

  1. Make a room of type miniboss (draw its spawn point with B).
  2. Give a floor Mini-bosses > 0 and a Mini-boss pool in the Floor Editor.

It spawns with that room's waves as adds; its waves keep coming while it lives, and the room clears only after the last add and the mini-boss are dead. It pays the Run Rules > Offers > Mini-boss offer, else the floor's Mini-boss drops loot table (mini-boss keeps loot also rolls the loot when an offer is set), but it never counts as a boss in records, unlocks or bossDamage.

A room can force one enemy (Mini-boss field). Floor plans use M for mini-boss rooms; an M plan with an empty mini-boss pool becomes a normal fight (Project Check shows it as an error).

docs.title: Effect blocks
docs.text: New words: WHEN boss_kill / miniboss_kill / elite_kill, DO enemy_modifier (id = modifier, on the target enemies), IF enemy_has_modifier. See Tools > Languages for the new strings, and Effect blocks for the system itself.

docs.title: Props, pits, gates and challenge rooms
Props
docs.text:
A prop is a room-layout character with a body (Tools > Dungeon Shooter Maker > Prop Editor): Layout char (reserved characters are refused), size, Blocks walking and Stops bullets, Health (0 = unbreakable), what it drops when it breaks and the effect blocks that run then, an Explodes flag (the old barrel: trap radius and damage, chains), hit/break animations and sounds, and your own sprite slot.

A flippable prop is cover: press E to turn it over, and with front blocking the flipped body only covers its Covered side, so bullets from the other side pass. The old props keep their characters, so every existing room still works: T table (flippable), P pillar, O pot (breaks in one hit), X barrel.

docs.title: Pits
docs.text: Paint ~ in a room layout for a hole in the floor. Falling costs Pit damage hearts (a fall never kills) and puts the hero back on the last safe square; a dodge roll crosses a one-tile pit. Enemies never step into pits. The Run Rules set the damage, the pause and the text; the look is a placeholder tile.

docs.title: Gates
docs.text:
A gate locks every door of a room until it opens: currency (pay keys/coins/your own money, or hold a key item), floor clear (every fight room done) or challenge (talking to the gate starts waves; beating them opens it). The interaction point stands on each doorway (E from either side).

Use a gated treasure room template, or let a floor lock N treasure rooms with Locked treasures (their own gate, else Run Rules > Default gate, 1 key by default); Extra gate chance can lock one more. A floor-clear gate on a fight room is a trap (Project Check warns).

docs.title: Challenge rooms
docs.text: A room of type challenge starts waves when entered: clear them within Seconds and without being hit (No hit) to get its loot table; a failure stops the waves, pays nothing and leaves whatever is on the floor to be finished (the room opens once it is empty). Fail can open the room, hurt, or retry once. Floors place Challenges in dead ends; drawn plans use C.

docs.title: Shopkeeper
docs.text: Give a shop a Keeper (an event): the shop room spawns that speaker (behind the counter by default), and talking uses the normal event pages, choices and effects. Stealing is left to your own events.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text:
You write content and UI in one language (English by default). Every other language is a table that says "this text → its translation". Tools > Dungeon Shooter Maker > Languages lists every text the game shows: names, descriptions, event dialogue, boss titles, the game title, and the UI words in code. English and Korean ship with the package.

  • Show: Missing lists what still needs a translation. Type it in the right column; anything left empty shows in the original language, so a half-done translation still plays.
  • Keep {0}, {1} ... in a translation: a number or a name goes there ({0} COINS → 코인 {0}). A translation that drops or adds one is marked red and the original is shown instead.
  • Export CSV / Import CSV go through a spreadsheet or a translator (columns: original, translation, where it is).
  • When you change a name or a line, its old translation becomes Unused and the new text Missing. Remove unused cleans up.
  • + Language adds a table. Set its code (ja, de ...): on first start the game picks the computer's language when there is a table for it; players change it under Settings > Language. Set a Font when the game fonts lack its letters (Japanese, Chinese ...).
  • Your own code: show text with Loc.T("TEXT") or Loc.T("{0} KEYS", n), and mark your own content fields [Localized]; both then appear in the window.

Project Check warns about missing translations and broken {0}s.

The game text uses the pixel font Galmuri (Galmuri7, Galmuri9 and Galmuri11 Bold, English and Korean), SIL Open Font License: it may ship with your game. Change the fonts and sizes in Runtime/Resources/DungeonShooterMaker/UI/Game.uss; keep pixel fonts at whole multiples of their pixel grid (the file lists them) so they stay sharp.

docs.title: Balance
docs.text:
Tools > Dungeon Shooter Maker > Balance shows the numbers behind your content for a chosen difficulty, computed the way the game computes them (nothing is played):

  • Coins & loot per floor: many runs (seeds) are planned floor by floor and their rewards averaged: rooms, fights, enemies, coins from room clears, enemy drops and loot, coins so far, chests, keys found against keys the chests need, hearts, items and guns, and the average price of a shop item. A short list flags floors where keys or coins fall short.
  • Gun damage: damage per shot, shots per second, damage per second over a clip and with reloads, all ammo, and the seconds each gun needs to kill the toughest normal enemy on each floor.
  • Enemy health & damage: health per floor (chart and table), bullet and touch damage, bullets per second, and the time to kill each enemy with a chosen gun.

Shrines, events, elites and item effects are not counted; mini-boss rooms are. Copy as CSV puts the table on the clipboard for a spreadsheet.

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
Assets/DungeonShooterMaker/
  Runtime/        game code (Core, Actors, Combat, Dungeon, Items, UI)
  Editor/         the maker windows
  Content/Default the sample game's assets
  Resources/      the content database
  Demo/           the demo scene (play mode starts here)
  Documentation/  this guide

Heroes, enemies, guns, effects and the game UI frames are sprite sheets (Content/Default and Resources). Floors, walls, props and some items and hazards are drawn from small pixel maps in code (Art.cs, ItemArt.cs, HazardArt). Any of them can be replaced from the sprite slots in the editors.

docs.title: The editors
docs.text: Every kind of content has its own window. This page lists what each one makes and then covers the parts they share: your own art, room layouts and secret rooms, drawn floor plans, effect blocks, and your own effects in C#.

docs.title: What each window makes
docs.text:
Editor What you make Run Rules Player basics (hearts, speed, roll), room-clear rewards and chest chance, shop prices, traps, curse/flair, hexed enemies, default hero, and OFFERS: which offer opens after a boss (instead of its loot, keeping its hearts, or as well), after a whole floor is cleared, or by chance after a room. LOBBY: the lobby floor and how many starting guns and items the loadout station adds. Heroes Playable characters: helmet/suit colors, hearts, speed, starting guns/items/keys/coins, extra stats. Two or more heroes turn on the hero select screen. Guns Fire mode (semi, auto, burst, charge), clip and ammo, spread, projectiles, bounce/pierce/homing/split/explode modifiers, status effects, effect blocks while held, quality and price, tags (e.g. pistol, ballistic) that gun upgrades and the gun_has_tag condition read. Live preview. Items Passive items (22 stats, mul and add), effect blocks (see below), and active items with rooms/seconds/damage recharge. Synergies "Holding A + B (+ any N of C, D, E) gives bonus stats and reactions." Announced in game with a SYNERGY! banner. Status Effects Burn, poison, freeze, chill, shock and your own: damage over time, slow, stacking, duration. Enemies & Bosses States with movement (chase, keep range, hop, dash, teleport, orbit, wander, still) and bullet patterns (aimed, radial, random, line, summon) with repeat/rotation (spirals), acceleration, curving, wave and homing. Bosses add HP-threshold phases and an intro card. The LIVE PATTERN preview plays your pattern in the window; 9 presets get you started. Elite chance × says whether this enemy can spawn as an elite. Elite Modifiers One elite prefix per enemy: health/speed/fire-delay/damage multipliers, extra bullet patterns (add to or replace the state's volleys), an aura of effect blocks, a sprite tint (outline colour/width are hooks), extra coins, hearts and loot, an appear animation and the default weight/floor range for elite pools. See Elites and mini-bosses. Crosshairs Aim marker looks: sprite slot or a drawn shape (cross, ring, tee, brackets), hotspot, tint, scale, spin, recoil/recovery, hide the system cursor. Run Rules picks one; a gun can name its own. Music Tracks by id: a loop clip (optionally an intro), volume and loop points. Run Rules, floors, rooms, bosses and phases pick them by id; an id with no asset is silence. See Music and sound. Sounds Sounds by id with one or more clips (one picked at random), volume and pitch variation. The 19 game sounds ship with recorded defaults; any id without a Sound asset uses the built-in generated sound. ▶ plays it. Effect Animations Animations from a sprite sheet or cut sprites: one-shot effects and looping ones (bullets, statuses). Run Rules pick one per event (34 events: shots, bullets in flight, hits, bounces, hurt, heal, death, teleport, summon, boss phase, pickups, chests, shrines, synergies, secret walls, events); guns, enemy attacks, enemies and status effects can pick their own. 42 defaults made with Pixel VFX Maker; only shell casings and dash dust are small code particles. Props Room props placed with one layout character: solid, bullet cover, breakable (health, loot drops, break effect blocks), flippable cover (one side stops bullets), or an exploding barrel. The four old props (T table, P pillar, O pot, X barrel) are built in. Rooms Paint layouts: walls of props, enemy spawns, boss and chest spots, spike traps (S), explosive barrels (X). Room type (start, normal, treasure, shop, boss, miniboss, shrine, event, secret, lobby), weight, floor range, enemy waves, and an extra elite chance. Lobby rooms add station spots 1-9, the exit hatch G and a stations table; mini-boss rooms take a spawn point (B), one forced enemy and their add waves. Floors Generated (room count, number of treasure/shrine/event/mini-boss/secret rooms, shop chance) or drawn by hand on a grid: pick a room kind, click squares, click between two rooms to join them. Enemy pool with weights per floor, boss pool, treasure chest, shop, boss loot, secret room loot, tile colors or your own floor and wall tiles. The preview shows each floor's enemy odds. Lobby turns a floor into the place between runs (only its look and name are used). Loot Tables Weighted entries (gun, item, coins, heart, ammo, key, purge, chest, nothing) with quality ranges, rolls, no-duplicates option. Used by chests, bosses, mimics and shrine challenges. Chests Quality, color, key cost, loot table, mimic chance and enemy, chance to break. Shops Shelf slots (kind + quality range or a fixed id) and a price multiplier. Prices come from Run Rules. Shrines Cost (coins, hearts, heart containers, keys, purges, curse, free), then instant effects (all or one at random), a lasting blessing, an item, or a challenge fight that drops a loot table. Events Someone to talk to in an event room: speaker name, color or your own sprite, pages of text and choices. A choice can need something (conditions, shown greyed out or hidden), cost coins/health/keys/curse, work by chance, run effect blocks, give an item or loot, start a fight, show a result line and go to another page. When the talk ends the speaker leaves, stays silent, or can be talked to again. Floors set how many event rooms they have. Currencies Coins and keys come built in; add your own (scrap, gems...). Name, short word in prices, icon (shape + color or your own sprite), pickup sound, HUD on/off and order, start amount, carry limit. Shop slots, shrines, event choices, chest locks and offer rerolls can cost any currency. PERSISTENCE: Kept between runs makes a persistent currency (start balance of a new save, bonuses per boss, new floor and won run); a run currency can carry a percent of what was earned or held into one. See Between runs. Offers Pick-N-of-M reward screens: how many cards are shown and picked, a weighted pool of rewards (perk, gun upgrade, item or gun by quality, a stat change, currency, healing, heart containers), reroll price (+ step, max) in any currency, and what skipping gives. Cards the hero can't use (a perk at its top level, an upgrade no held gun fits) are left out. ▶ Try this offer opens it in a test room. Run Rules open offers after a boss, when every fight room of a floor is cleared, or by chance after a room; shrines, events and items open them with the offer effect. Upgrades Hero perks (for the rest of the run) and gun upgrades (on one gun: any gun, one gun, or every gun with a tag). Each level adds stats and effect blocks on top of the levels before it. Weight and first floor for random picks. Taken perks show in the HUD tray with their level; upgraded guns show +N next to their name and in the pause screen. Meta upgrades are bought in the lobby with a persistent currency and apply to every run: requirements (a talent tree), group (shop column) and order, a price and the content each level opens. The preview shows the whole meta shop. Difficulties Levels the player picks on the hero screen (▲ ▼): enemy health (also per floor and for bosses), speed, fire rate, bullet damage, extra enemies per wave, elite chance, shop prices and the hero's own stats. The first open one is the default. Unlocks Goals counted over all runs (runs played or won, best floor, enemies, bosses, coins, a win with a hero or on a difficulty) that open locked content: guns, items, heroes, difficulties, events, chests, shrines. Locked content never drops or shows up. The editor also shows and resets the save used when testing in the editor.

Every list editor has New / Duplicate / Delete / Ping, a search box, and a preview panel on the right.

docs.title: Your own art
docs.text:
Guns, bullets, enemies, heroes, items and chests have a Your sprite slot. Leave it empty to keep the built-in art. Fill it with a sprite sheet (PNG, set the frame width/height; frames run left to right, top to bottom) or a list of cut sprites. More than one frame plays as an animation (enemies and heroes walk, bullets spin). Art is drawn facing right at 16 pixels per tile whatever the import settings; the pivot is the point that sits on the object's position. Your art keeps its own colors (the built-in shapes are tinted). There is no drawing tool: use your usual pixel editor.

A gun sprite can give its Grip point (held in the hero's hand) and Muzzle point (where bullets and the muzzle animation leave), in pixels from the sprite's top-left; -1 keeps the sprite's pivot as the grip and fires from just in front of the hero. Guns drawn at 32 pixels per unit (set it in the slot) look big and chunky in hand.

docs.title: Motion sheets (Pixel Legion Maker)
docs.text:
Heroes and enemies can also use a motion sheet: one row per motion, with a .json beside the PNG naming each row (idle, running, attack, damaged, death; fps, frameWidth, frameHeight, and the feet point originX / groundPx). Pixel Legion Maker writes exactly this with every hero export (Exports/Heroes/HERO_name.png + .json): drop the PNG in Sheet and the motions, 32 pixels per unit and the left-facing flag fill in.

The game plays idle/running from movement, attack when firing, damaged when hit and death before the body fades; a hero's roll row plays during the dodge roll (the gun is put away). Missing motions fall back (running → walk → idle). The two crowned bosses were made with Pixel Legion Maker; for heroes, export without a weapon so they hold the game's gun.

A hero sheet can say where the gun hand is: handX / handY (pixels from a frame's top-left, drawn facing as the sheet faces), and per row handX / handY lists (one point per frame, -1 = the sheet's point) so the gun follows the arm. Any sheet works the same way if you write the .json by hand. Low-res render mode draws 32-pixel art at the game's 16-pixel grid, so fine detail is lost there.

Effects (Pixel VFX Maker). Drop a Pixel VFX Maker export (name.png with name.sheet.json beside it) in any sheet slot and the frame size, count, speed, looping and pivot fill in.

Floors take floor tiles and wall tiles the same way: 16x16 px each. With several frames the first is the plain tile (used half the time) and the others are mixed in at random. Textures don't need Read/Write enabled.

docs.title: Secret rooms
docs.text: A secret room sits behind a faintly cracked wall. Any explosion near the wall (a bomb item, an explosive bullet, a barrel) opens it: the doorway and its corridor appear and the room shows on the map. Inside is a random chest, or the floor's secret room loot spilled when it opens. Generated floors place Secret rooms of them next to plain or special rooms (never the start or the boss room); in a drawn plan, a ? room joined to a room is secret.

docs.title: Drawn floor plans
docs.text:
A drawn plan is saved as text in the floor (JSON: layout), one string per row. Rooms sit on even positions, - joins rooms sideways and | up and down:

S-N-N
| | |
? T-B
  |
  E

S start, N fight, B boss, T treasure, $ shop, H shrine, E event (a fight when no event fits), ? secret. Plans also use C for challenge rooms and M for mini-boss rooms.

A plan needs one start and one boss, every room joined, and the boss reachable without secret rooms. A broken plan is reported by the Floor Editor and Project Check, and the floor is generated instead until it is fixed.

Tools > Dungeon Shooter Maker > Advanced > Rebuild Default Sounds and Effects recreates the default Sound and Effect assets from Sounds/Default and Vfx/Default (your own assets are left alone).

docs.title: Effect blocks: WHEN → IF → DO
docs.text:
Items, synergies, guns (while held), shrines and boss phases share one system.

WHEN an event happens: room_clear, kill, hit (a player bullet hits an enemy), damaged, roll, purge, reload, shot, room_enter, floor_start, pickup (items only), offer_picked (a card was taken on an offer screen), run_start (once, after the hero, starting gear and meta upgrades are applied). Chance and Every Nth thin it out; Every Nth counts only events whose conditions passed. Elites add boss_kill, miniboss_kill and elite_kill (see Elites and mini-bosses).

IF every condition passes (each can be flipped with NOT): hp_below, hp_full, coins_at_least, keys_at_least, has (a gun or item), boss_room, enemies_at_least, clip_empty, floor_at_least, stat_at_least, event_boss, upgrade_level (a perk, or a gun upgrade on the current gun, at least level N), gun_has_tag, currency_at_least.

DO the effects. Effects that pick enemies or a place have a Target: event (the enemy that was hit or killed), nearest, random, all, player, or source (the boss, in phase effects). If the event's enemy already died (a killing hit), event picks nobody. Effects: heal, max_hp, coins, keys, purges, ammo, reload, invulnerable, damage, damage_room, status, status_room, explode, bullet_ring, clear_bullets, toast, offer (opens an offer screen), upgrade_gun and grant_perk (a named or random one), currency (gives any currency), grant_item (a named item, or a random one when empty), grant_gun (a named gun).

Boss phases offer only effects that work from a boss: bullet_ring and explode (hurt the player), damage (hurts the player), heal (the boss), clear_bullets, toast.

Examples in the default content: Static Coil (WHEN hit, 20% → shock the enemy that was hit), Last Stand Locket (WHEN entering a room IF below 2 hearts → 3 s invulnerable + "LAST STAND"), Old Iron (WHEN reloading IF the clip is empty → ring of 8 bullets), Gale Vulture phase 2 (a ring of 16 bullets from the boss).

Effects never start more events while they run, and bullets made by effects never count as hit, so blocks cannot loop forever.

docs.title: Your own effects in C# (no editor changes needed)
docs.text:
Write a class with a parameterless constructor that implements IEffectType, IConditionType or ITriggerType anywhere in your project. It is found automatically and its id appears in every effect, condition and event dropdown. See Demo/Extensions/ExampleExtensions.cs:

public class ChainZapEffect : IEffectType
{
    public string Id => "chain_zap";
    public string Uses => "amount damage to the target, then jumps to count more enemies within radius";
    public string DefaultTarget => Target.Event;
    public bool SupportsHostile => false; // true = also offered in boss phases (ctx.Hostile: hurt the player)
    public void Run(ItemEffectDef e, EffectContext ctx) { /* ctx.Enemies(e.target, Target.Event), ctx.Player, ctx.Point ... */ }
}

EffectContext gives the player, the event's enemy, the event point, the room and Enemies(target) / PointOf(target). Fire your own event from any script with EffectLibrary.FireTrigger("my_event"). Ids must be unique; clashes are listed by Project Check.

docs.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
docs.text: This page covers testing, the project-wide check, the design rules the sample follows, and the problems people hit most often with answers taken from the manual.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Each editor's ▶ button starts play mode in a fitting test room with the thing you are editing: gun or item in hand, enemy or boss in the arena, chest in a treasure room, shrine in a shrine room, hero chosen.

Built players accept the same tests on the command line, which is handy for automated checks:

Game.exe -testroom <room id> -gun <id> -item <id> -enemy <id> -chest <id> -shrine <id> -character <id>
         -coins N -keys N -hexed -content <json folder> -demo

-difficulty <id> plays on that difficulty; -progress <file> uses that save file, -unlockall opens everything, -progresstest checks unlocks, difficulty, the save and the win screen (use a test save file). -event <id> puts that event in event rooms; -eventtest runs a talk through the dialogue window. -arttest checks sounds, effect animations and sprite slots. -demo plays the game by itself (moves, shoots, picks up loot).

-autoshot file.png -shotdelay S saves a screenshot and quits; the log lists [event] lines for everything that happened (items picked, patterns fired, synergies, loot).

docs.title: Project Check
docs.text:
Project Overview ▸ Check project lists:

  • Errors: data the game cannot load (the same messages as the editors).
  • Warnings: content that can never appear (enemies in no floor, items nobody can get, rooms allowed on no floor), floors without a boss or enemies, loot tables asking for a quality no gun/item has, synergies that need unobtainable gear, meta upgrades that are free or priced in a run currency, persistent currencies nothing gives, lobby rooms without a hero station or with spot numbers that have no station. A lobby room without an exit G is an error.
  • Notes: things that work but fall back to defaults (no shop picked, no shrine room template, one hero only).

Each line has an Open button that jumps to the asset.

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• Rewards follow the genre's pity system: every cleared room without a chest raises the next room's chest chance by a step, up to a cap. Flair raises it further; curse raises mimic and hexed chances.
  • Quality runs D, C, B, A, S. Chests, shops and loot tables pick by quality range and prefer things the player does not own yet.
  • Bosses pause on an intro card, then switch states at HP thresholds; each phase can clear bullets, grant brief invulnerability and speed up.
  • Waves: a normal room with Enemy waves > 1 spawns the next wave after the previous one is beaten.

docs.title: My content does not load, or the game skips an entry
docs.text: That is the designed behaviour: the game never loads broken data, reports the problem and skips that entry. The editors show the same message at the top of the form. Fix the error, or read the Errors list in Project Check.

docs.title: My JSON edit does nothing
docs.text: A built game reads JSON from Application.persistentDataPath/content/ (or a folder passed with -content <dir>), and files there override default content by id. Check that the id in your file matches the asset you meant to change, and that you are looking at the folder the build actually reads. See Mods and JSON.

docs.title: My drawn floor plan is ignored
docs.text: A plan needs one start and one boss, every room joined, and the boss reachable without secret rooms. A broken plan is reported by the Floor Editor and Project Check, and the floor is generated instead until it is fixed.

docs.title: A mini-boss room plays as a normal fight
docs.text: An M room in a drawn plan, or a floor with Mini-bosses > 0, needs a Mini-boss pool (or a forced Mini-boss enemy in the room). An M plan with an empty mini-boss pool becomes a normal fight, and Project Check shows it as an error. See Mini-bosses.

docs.title: The hero select screen does not appear
docs.text: The hero select screen needs two or more heroes. With one hero the run starts with that hero, and Project Check notes it as a fallback.

docs.title: The lobby does not appear
docs.text: Run Rules ▸ Lobby must name a floor made with Lobby on in the Floor Editor. A lobby room needs the exit hatch G (missing it is an error) and a hero station is expected (Project Check warns without one). With the field empty there is no lobby: the title leads to hero select and the run as usual. See The lobby.

docs.title: The game is silent
docs.text: No music tracks ship: the sample is silent until you add tracks in the Music Editor, and an id with no asset is silence. For one-shot sounds, any id without a Sound asset uses the built-in generated sound. Check Settings for Master, Music and Sfx volume. See Music and sound.

docs.title: My translation does not show
docs.text: An empty translation shows the original language, so a half-done translation still plays. A translation that drops or adds a {0} placeholder is marked red and the original is shown instead; Project Check also warns about missing translations and broken {0}s. See Languages.

docs.title: A secret room will not open
docs.text: A secret room sits behind a faintly cracked wall and opens when an explosion happens near it: a bomb item, an explosive bullet or a barrel. Opening it makes the doorway and corridor appear and the room show on the map. See Secret rooms.

docs.title: My 32-pixel art lost detail
docs.text: Low-res render mode draws 32-pixel art at the game's 16-pixel grid, so fine detail is lost there. Import art at the grid you want to see, or turn the mode off. See Your own art.

docs.title: My gun sprite sits wrong in the hand
docs.text: Set the gun sprite's Grip point and Muzzle point (pixels from the sprite's top-left); -1 keeps the sprite's pivot as the grip and fires from just in front of the hero. Guns drawn at 32 pixels per unit look big and chunky in hand. See Your own art.

docs.title: CONTINUE is missing or the run is refused
docs.text: A snapshot is written when a floor starts, and the title shows CONTINUE while it exists. Death, a win and starting a new run delete it; quitting to the title keeps it. An old version or a changed project is refused with a message — Run Rules > Saving sets the mismatch policy. See Resuming a run.

docs.title: An effect loops forever
docs.text: Effects never start more events while they run, and bullets made by effects never count as hit, so blocks cannot loop forever. If an effect seems to repeat, look at its WHEN event and its Every Nth setting in Effect blocks.

docs.title: Content never appears in a run
docs.text: Project Check warns about enemies in no floor, items nobody can get, rooms allowed on no floor, loot tables asking for a quality no gun or item has, synergies that need unobtainable gear and unlocked content that never drops. Locked content never drops or shows up — check the Unlocks editor and any meta upgrade that opens it.

docs.title: Music and sound
docs.text: Three editors cover audio and animation: Music for tracks, Sounds for one-shot sounds, and Effect Animations for the sprites that play on events. All three are picked by id from data, so nothing needs code.

docs.title: Music
docs.text:
Add tracks in the Music Editor: a loop clip, an optional intro, and loop points.

Run Rules pick the title, lobby, default floor, boss, mini-boss, challenge, shop, shrine and event tracks and the stingers (boss intro, boss defeated, victory, death, elite appears).

A floor, a room template, a boss and a boss phase can each name their own track. The ladder is:

phase → boss/mini-boss → room → room type → floor → default

Changes crossfade, the music ducks under the pause menu and offers and while a stinger plays. An id with no asset is silence. The sample ships 10 looping tracks and 5 stingers (Content/Default/Music); replace them or add your own.

docs.title: Sounds
docs.text:
Sounds by id with one or more clips (one picked at random), volume and pitch variation.

  • The 19 game sounds ship with recorded defaults.
  • Any id without a Sound asset uses the built-in generated sound.
  • ▶ plays the sound in the editor.

Volumes live in Settings: Master, Music and Sfx (the old volume setting is the master).

docs.title: Effect Animations
docs.text:
Animations from a sprite sheet or cut sprites: one-shot effects and looping ones (bullets, statuses).

  • Run Rules pick one per event: 34 events cover shots, bullets in flight, hits, bounces, hurt, heal, death, teleport, summon, boss phase, pickups, chests, shrines, synergies, secret walls and events.
  • Guns, enemy attacks, enemies and status effects can pick their own.
  • 42 defaults were made with Pixel VFX Maker; only shell casings and dash dust are small code particles.

Rebuild defaults. Tools > Dungeon Shooter Maker > Advanced > Rebuild Default Sounds and Effects recreates the default Sound and Effect assets from Sounds/Default and Vfx/Default (your own assets are left alone).

docs.text:

  • Run rules and progression — the Run Rules side of music and game feel.
  • Support and licenses — the font and sound credits that ship with the package.

docs.title: 1. Open the overview
docs.text:
Open Tools ▸ Dungeon Shooter Maker ▸ Project Overview. It opens by itself the first time the package loads.

The overview shows one card per kind of content (heroes, guns, items, enemies, rooms, floors, music and so on) and counts what the project contains. Every card opens its editor.

docs.title: 2. Play the sample
docs.text:
Press ▶ Play the game. The demo scene opens and a run starts with the hero select screen.

Two or more heroes turn the hero select screen on; with one hero the run starts with that hero.

docs.title: 3. Change one value and test it
docs.text:
Open any editor from the overview cards, change a value and press its ▶ button to test that one thing. For example, ▶ Try this gun drops you in a room holding the gun; an enemy's ▶ spawns it in the arena.

Each editor's ▶ starts play mode in a fitting test room with the thing you are editing: gun or item in hand, enemy or boss in the arena, chest in a treasure room, shrine in a shrine room, hero chosen.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Input Action WASD move mouse aim left click fire Space dodge roll R reload Q purge F active item E interact (buy, open, use shrine) mouse wheel, Tab / 1 / 2 switch gun

docs.title: Where your content lives
docs.text:
Each piece of content is a ScriptableObject asset (Assets/DungeonShooterMaker/Content/Default/...) listed in the Content Database (Resources/DungeonShooterMaker/DefaultContent). Every asset has an id (lower case, used for references) and a name (shown to the player).

Editors check your data as you type. Problems show at the top of the form, and the game never loads broken data: it reports the problem and skips that entry. Undo works for every edit.

See How content works for the asset model, Mods and JSON for the export/import folder names, and Project Check for the project-wide audit.

docs.title: Run rules and progression
docs.text: Tools ▸ Dungeon Shooter Maker ▸ Run Rules holds the rules the whole run shares: what the hero starts with, what rooms pay, what things cost, how curse and flair work, which enemies can be elite, which offer opens when, and the lobby between runs.

docs.title: What Run Rules set
docs.text:
• Player basics: hearts, speed, roll.
  • Rewards: room-clear rewards and chest chance, shop prices, traps.
  • Curse and flair.
  • Hexed enemies (old content; see Elites and mini-bosses).
  • Default hero.
  • Offers: which offer opens after a boss (instead of its loot, keeping its hearts, or as well), after a whole floor is cleared, or by chance after a room.
  • Lobby: the lobby floor and how many starting guns and items the loadout station adds.

docs.title: Offers
docs.text:
An offer is a pick-N-of-M reward screen made in the Offers editor: how many cards are shown and picked, a weighted pool of rewards (perk, gun upgrade, item or gun by quality, a stat change, currency, healing, heart containers), a reroll price (+ step, max) in any currency, and what skipping gives.

Cards the hero can't use (a perk at its top level, an upgrade no held gun fits) are left out. ▶ Try this offer opens it in a test room.

Offers open from:

  • Run Rules — after a boss, when every fight room of a floor is cleared, or by chance after a room.
  • Shrines, events and items — with the offer effect.
  • Mini-bosses — the mini-boss offer, when one is set.

docs.title: Elites
docs.text:
An elite is a normal enemy that spawns with one modifier. The modifier itself (numbers, extra patterns, aura, tint, drops, prefix) is an asset made in the Elite Modifiers editor and described in Elites and mini-bosses. Run Rules control how often they appear.

Run Rules > Elites sets:

  • the base chance,
  • a guaranteed number per floor,
  • whether bosses can be elite,
  • a chance-by-curse curve (empty = the old hexed curve),
  • a weighted pool of modifiers (empty = the built-in hexed one).

Other places add to it: a floor can add its own chance and pool in the Floor Editor, a difficulty has Elite chance +, a room has Extra elite chance in this room, and an encounter line with Elite on always spawns elites (a wave of them). Rolls use the floor's seed, so -seed reproduces the same elites.

Old hexed content. Run Rules > Hexed enemies still exists for content written before elite modifiers: its numbers become the built-in hexed modifier (no name prefix and the old "hexed enemy appears" effect, so old enemies look the same), and Convert these numbers to a hexed modifier asset turns them into a real one you can edit.

docs.title: Persistent currencies
docs.text:
In the Currency Editor, turn on Kept between runs. Its balance lives in the save: a new save starts with the start balance, and the currency can be given while playing like any other (loot tables, offers, the currency effect) plus fixed bonuses per boss, per new floor (from floor 2) and per won run. In a run the HUD shows it; the balance is saved when the run ends.

A run currency (coins, your own) can feed one: set Carry into, a Carry percent (0-100) and what the percent is taken of: earned (everything picked up this run, so spending in shops is not punished) or held (what is left at the end). Banking happens on death and on a win; restarting or quitting a run banks nothing. The hero stat carryOver multiplies what is banked. The preview shows an example ("a run earning 300 Coins banks 30 Glints").

docs.title: Meta upgrades
docs.text:
In the Upgrade Editor, set scope meta. Each level has a price (use a persistent currency), stats and effect blocks like a perk, and can open content that stays locked until it is bought (guns, items, heroes, difficulties, events, chests, shrines, offers, upgrades; locked content does not drop either). Levels add up and apply at the start of every run; WHEN run_start blocks are the usual way to give starting coins or gear (grant_item, grant_gun).

Requirements make a talent tree: every listed upgrade must be owned at its level before level I can be bought. Group is the column of the lobby shop and order the row in it. The preview draws the whole shop, with the requirements as "needs X II".

docs.title: The lobby
docs.text:
A place the player walks around between runs:

  1. Make a room of type lobby in the Room Editor. Paint station spots 1-9 and the exit hatch G (stepping onto it starts the run; put it away from the stations). Fill the Stations table: each station stands on a spot and either opens an event (a talk; a choice's Opens screen opens a lobby screen when the talk ends) or opens a screen directly. Label is the prompt; look is the built-in figure or prop (speaker, altar, pedestal, table, pillar, pot) and tint colors it; Your sprite for this station takes a sprite, a sheet or a motion sheet instead.
  2. Make a floor with Lobby on in the Floor Editor: only its look (colors or tiles) and name are used; its room is the first lobby room in its room list, or the first lobby room.
  3. Pick that floor in Run Rules ▸ Lobby. Empty = no lobby: the title leads to hero select and the run as before.

Screens: meta_shop (buy meta upgrades), hero (hero and difficulty for the next run), difficulty, records (totals, unlocks, recent runs) and loadout (starting gear). Without a hero station the hero stays the last one played; Project Check warns about it.

docs.title: Starting gear picks
docs.text: Guns and items with Start pick on can be chosen at the loadout station (once open). They are added to the hero's own kit: Run Rules set how many guns and items (Start gun picks, Start item picks), and a hero can set its own numbers (-1 = Run Rules).

docs.title: Game feel
docs.text:
Run Rules > Game Feel.

  • Hit stop freezes the world for a moment when a bullet lands (longer on a kill, an elite or a boss phase; the longest request wins, capped). It never fights a menu, an offer or the pause screen, and it always restores the time scale.
  • Damage numbers float off the target (repeated hits on the same enemy merge for a moment, the list is capped; the colour separates the hero's hits from damage taken).
  • Low health turns on under a fraction of max health (or at one heart) and pulses with an optional sound once per episode.
  • Aim assist is pad-only: a target inside the cone and range pulls the aim while the mouse is never helped; strength 0 turns it off.
  • Shake scale multiplies screen shake on top of the player's setting.

The crosshair comes from the Crosshair Editor (Run Rules picks one, a gun may override it); its look and the damage numbers/low-health vignette are drawn by the UI pass and only read these rules.

docs.title: Resuming a run
docs.text:
A snapshot (run.json) is written when a floor starts, and the title shows CONTINUE while it exists. It stores the seed, floor, hero, difficulty, wallets, the run's numbers, health, guns (with clip/reserve and gun upgrades), passives/active item and perks; the floor itself is rebuilt from the seed, so enemies and opened chests are not stored.

Death, a win and starting a new run delete it; quitting to the title keeps it, and an old version or a changed project is refused with a message (Run Rules > Saving sets the mismatch policy). A resumed run keeps its time and stats and counts in the records (marked as resumed). Demo and test runs never write the real save; -run <file> points the tests at their own file.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://hyunter777.github.io/dungeon-shooter-maker-docs/
  • Q&A: https://github.com/hyunter777/dungeon-shooter-maker-docs/discussions/categories/q-a
  • Bug reports: https://github.com/hyunter777/dungeon-shooter-maker-docs/issues
  • Publisher website: https://www.flycat.co.kr
  • Email: hyunter@flycat.co.kr

Ask usage and integration questions in Q&A, and report reproducible defects through the bug report form in Issues.

For a reproducible issue, include the product version, full Unity Editor version, render pipeline, operating system, the content id or window involved, reproduction steps, expected and actual behaviour and the relevant Console messages. A screenshot is useful.

Public posts are visible to everyone: remove personal information, credentials and private project paths, and do not upload the purchased package, the product implementation, the sample content as a package, fonts or a complete customer project. Use private support to arrange any necessary confidential reproduction details.

These destinations are prepared for publication. This support policy does not promise a response time or announce product availability.
